George Oliver, carrying on his good form, held third place the whole way, and Harry Shields, who came along during the latter half, just managed to hold Fred Rolfe out of 4th place, but Fred's fine walk won him the handicap.
The race opened with George Oliver going into the lead, followed by George Beecham, who was tackling his first 20, Hugh McGreechan, out to hold his title, and George Checkley, all together.
In the Club 2 mile walk handicap we saw a new young member, R. Middleton, make good use of his long start to come home an easy winner from Eric Hall, with George Oliver third.
The 2 miles walk handicap was won by Eric Hall, with George Oliver second and L. Demmon third, and the back-markers did not seem to have much chance of catching their field.

McMullen won the 2 miles Walk, after a long string of second places, and his time of 15 mins. 5.4 secs. was quite good after his lay-off during the winter season. G. Oliver was second, with Syd James in third place.
George Oliver won the Civil Service 2 miles Track Championship on July 18th. Gerry Warr has now gone into the R.A.F. for his National Service.
